Thanks Samir — answers below and quick guidance so engineering can proceed:  

- Redaction: prefer client-side token replacement for anything regulated (PII, SSNs, ticket IDs). Our recommended approach:
  - Replace exact customer identifiers with stable placeholders (e.g., <CUSTOMER_ID_1>) to preserve referential structure.
  - For free-text PII (emails, phone numbers) we recommend regex-based masking before upload.
  - We can also accept the CSV with a "raw" column if you want Redwood to run redaction in a separate, auditable step — note this requires an NDA addendum for logging raw values.

- Recommended models:
  - KG-grounded responses (longer context, higher fidelity): rdx-large-v2 (recommended starting point) or rdx-xlarge-1 if you need higher factuality at cost.
  - Short-form classification/triage: rdx-medium-1 (cheaper ops, lower latency).
  - For cost-sensitive throughput: rdx-medium-1 quantized (int8) or rdx-small-1 for high-volume triage.

- Lightweight benchmark: usually 2–6 hours depending on size of prompt set (most pilots complete in ~3 hours). We run: exact-match/EM, F1 where applicable, and a short qualitative pass on a 100-prompt sample. Full eval results + recommended quantization options follow in the report.

Attachments: redaction_guidelines.pdf
Benchmarks: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026

Rafael will follow up with a short list of edge-case prompts we typically ask for and a sample prompt set we use internally for the CS triage pilot.

Best,
Marissa

Hey Samir — quick note from the solutions side:  

To speed the model-fit analysis, a few additional edge-case buckets are really helpful:  
- Ambiguity: prompts that lack context and could map to multiple intents.
- Long context churn: customer messages with long quoted histories and metadata.
- Mixed language: short prompts that switch languages mid-sentence.
- Hallucination-prone: prompts requiring numeric or temporal reasoning (dates, prices).
- Redaction complexity: prompts where identifiers are embedded inside code snippets or free-form notes.

If you can flag 8–12 examples across those buckets that would be ideal. We'll also run a prompt-perturbation sweep (typos, truncated sentences) to validate robustness.

I'll draft a short example CSV with sample entries and post it to the shared folder later today. If you prefer, drop the completed file in the folder and we'll pick it up.

-Rafael
